title: Clean up orphaned photo files
description: Buried finding from LODGY-11/LODGY-28: PhotoStorage persists a picked/captured image to app-private storage immediately, before the tenant form is ever saved. An abandoned pick (form closed without saving, or interrupted) leaves a permanently dangling file that nothing ever cleans up - these accumulate over time and get included in every future backup export (LODGY-28) even though no record references them.
acceptanceCriteria: A cleanup routine runs automatically on app start (on a background dispatcher, not blocking startup) - no manual maintenance action needed - and identifies photo files under filesDir/photos not referenced by any tenant's photoPath/idProofPhotoPath, then deletes them
Referenced photos are never touched by the cleanup, verified against real tenant records including vacated tenants
Backup export (LODGY-28) no longer includes orphaned files after cleanup has run

history.note: Added from the v2 feedback session (warden interviews after the v1 field test) and from buried enhancement/limitation notes surfaced while re-reading the full v1 board history.
Resolved: run automatically on app start, not as a manual action a warden would have to remember to trigger.
Starting - an app-start sweep on a background dispatcher that deletes files under filesDir/photos referenced by no tenant's photoPath or idProofPhotoPath.

Added media/OrphanPhotoCleaner.kt, run fire-and-forget from LodgyApplication.onCreate() on Dispatchers.IO so startup never waits on a directory listing and a sweep that races a fresh pick simply finds that file referenced on the next launch - no manual action anywhere. It reads every tenant, vacated included (a checked-out tenant's ID proof is still a live reference), collects photoPath and idProofPhotoPath, and deletes anything under filesDir/photos not in that set. Matching is by file name rather than the stored absolute path: LODGY-29's restore copies photos back by name while the DB keeps whatever path the old install wrote, so a full-path comparison would declare a freshly restored library entirely orphaned and delete every photo the warden has - the exact failure this ticket must not introduce. Because the sweep runs before an export, LODGY-28's zip stops carrying dangling files (AC 3). OrphanPhotoCleanerTest runs against a real TemporaryFolder and covers the keep/delete split, ID-proof-only references, vacated tenants, the restored-under-a-different-path case, empty and missing directories, and the no-tenants case. testDebugUnitTest green (322 tests).
